query: Louisiana psychologists and psychiatrists likely to write an independent medical opinion (nexus letter) for an MST-based PTSD VA service-connection claim
decision_informed: Which doctoral-level provider to commission for an IMO/nexus letter, and how to verify they are licensed and credible to VA
assumptions: Veteran splits time between Texas and Louisiana (veteran-profile.md:69); scope = providers seen in person in Louisiana or by telehealth while the veteran is physically in Louisiana
Telehealth licensure follows the patient's physical location; Texas-located sessions need TX licensure or PSYPACT authority
Doctoral psychologists (PhD/PsyD) and psychiatrists (MD/DO) only; LPC/LCSW/NP excluded as authors because they add weight problems this claim already has
Case complications the provider must handle: delayed MST disclosure, five prior trauma denials, pre-service history/soundness, substance use (incl. kratom/7-OH) as secondary
VA-weighting criteria taken from IMO-PROVIDER-RESEARCH-2026-10-12.md section 1 (citations verified 2026-10-19); not re-researched
angles: A1 Louisiana licensure and telehealth rules (LSBEP, PSYPACT status, LSBME telemedicine) for a TX/LA veteran
A2 Louisiana doctoral psychologists offering VA PTSD/MST IMOs, nexus letters or DBQs
A3 Louisiana psychiatrists / forensic psychiatrists offering VA IMOs
A4 Louisiana free or low-cost routes (law-school veterans clinics, LDVA, nonprofits)
A5 License-verification paths and disciplinary checks for candidates
